title: Introduce RAG step-serializer quickstart and delta authoring guide
author: Sofia Martinez
release_notes: Adds a new quickstart for serializing RAG session steps and a small delta-authoring pattern to optimize telemetry and replay storage. No runtime behavior changes.
body:
Background and motivation:
This PR adds a compact quickstart that demonstrates how to capture, serialize, and replay RAG session steps using a step-serializer + delta-authoring pattern. The goal is to provide teams with a low-friction example for emitting step-level telemetry and producing compact session artifacts that can be shipped to offline evaluators or ingested by the replay tooling. It complements existing RAG playbooks by focusing on storage-efficient session artifacts and deterministic step deltas for long-running multi-tool conversations.

What this PR contains:
- A new doc page under docs/quickstarts/rag-step-serializer.md with a step-by-step tutorial and code snippets (Node + Python).
- Example library: examples/rag-step-serializer/{index.js,serializer.py,fixtures/} showing a tiny serializer that emits per-step deltas and compresses stable prefixes.
- A short authoring guide (docs/recipes/delta-authoring.md) describing tradeoffs for delta size, determinism, and replay fidelity.
- Small additions to the telemetry schema examples so teams can map step ids to traces for end-to-end debugging.

Why this is different from our other quickstarts:
Rather than presenting a full RAG orchestration or a devcontainer, this quickstart is intentionally minimal and orthogonal: it teaches a pattern for representing sessions as a sequence of typed step deltas (input, tool-calls, model-outputs, attachments) and showcases a tiny serializer implementation you can drop into any agent. The serializer is opinionated (append-only, stable step ids, prefer prefix snapshots every N steps) to make replay and diffs cheap.

Small illustrative snippet (from index.js):
const { StepSerializer } = require('./serializer');
const s = new StepSerializer({ snapshotEvery: 50 });
// capture an input step
s.append({ type: 'input', id: s.nextId(), payload: { text: 'Find sources for pricing' } });
// capture a tool call and model output as deltas
s.append({ type: 'tool_call', id: s.nextId(), payload: { name: 'search', args: ['pricing'] } });

Notes for maintainers and docs writers:
- This example is intentionally small; do not expand the fixtures in the repo. If teams want to adapt pattern to production, point them at delta-authoring.md which lists operational concerns (indexing, retention, rehydration strategy).
- The serializer is permissive by design: it assumes the caller will sign/etag snapshots if they care about integrity.
- Consider adding the quickstart to the next docs patch release; I added a short release note above.
